item.title: CVE-2026-130349 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3
item.description: Tuesday 17 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3 | phpMyFAQ from 4.2.0-alpha.2 before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows category- or language-restricted editors to bypass scoped rights via public REST write endpoints. Attackers with a scoped right and the shared API token can use PUT faq/update, POST faq/create, and POST category to rewrite published FAQs and create root categories outside their scope.

item.title: CVE-2026-130350 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.1
item.description: Tuesday 17 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.1 | phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows delegated group or user admins to remove rights they do not hold by submitting empty rights lists. Attackers can send an empty rightIds or userRights array to group/permissions or user/update-rights to wipe all rights of more-privileged groups or administrators.

item.title: CVE-2026-130351 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1
item.description: Tuesday 17 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1 | phpMyFAQ from 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the multisite Redis configuration store that is not tenant-scoped. As a result, tenant administrators can read and overwrite the master instance's effective configuration. Attackers can save configuration through /admin/api/configuration, optionally resetting storage.redisPrefix, to redirect master SMTP, set a known API token, or alter authentication settings.

item.title: CVE-2026-130352 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9

item.title: CVE-2026-130353 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9

item.title: CVE-2026-130354 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9

item.title: CVE-2026-130361 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7

item.title: CVE-2026-125275 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.2
item.description:
Tuesday 17 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.2 | Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') vulnerability in device certificate verification in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service via a TLS client certificate whose CA is not registered. When a client certificate chains to a root in the device endpoint's trust store but no CA in the chain is registered in NervesHub, NervesHub.SSL.decide/2 refuses it with the reason :unknown_ca. Erlang/OTP ssl reads that reason as a missing trust anchor, looks for an alternative root, finds the same root and validates again without end. The handshake process queries the database on each pass and keeps running after the client disconnects, until the node restarts.
The device endpoint trusts the public roots from CAStore unless DEVICE_SSL_CACERTFILE is set, so a client certificate from a public CA whose chain allows client authentication is sufficient. A chain that ends at a root outside the trust store is refused once.
This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.4.
